newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Central Bank to ease T-bill trade terms.
newsitem.headline: Russia Central Bank to ease T-bill trade terms.

text.p: The Central Bank said on Thursday that it would ease terms of currency deals by foreigners trading Treasury bills from April 2.

It said the amount of cash deals required to be carried out with the Central Bank when foreigners holding special accounts transferred money into Russia to purchase T-bills would fall to 40 percent from 50 percent.
The proportion of forward transactions to repatriate funds required to be carried out with the bank would fall to 50 percent from 65 percent, it said.
Foreigners investing in government securities must buy roubles in special "S" accounts from Russian banks, from which they can repatriate profits through forwards and options deals.

The bank said that the guaranteed dollar yield for foreigners purchasing forward currency contracts at the same time as the securities and holding the securities to maturity would remain 12.5 percent.
Russian T-bills offer some of the world's highest emerging market returns, with one-year T-bills yielding around 37 percent on Thursday, down from close to 200 percent early last year.

The Central Bank influences the overall yield in dollar terms available to non-residents by requiring Russian banks operating the accounts to offset a proportion of the cash purchases and forward sales with it at non-market rates.
The bank has promised that foreigners will be given equal treatment on the government securities market by the end of the year.
Bank deputy chairman Andrei Kozlov on Wednesday said that the period of forwards for repatriation would be reduced to one to three days from two months by the beginning of next year.
